name: Scientific socialism
summary: Scientific socialism is the Marx-Engels doctrine that socialism is the outcome of the historical development of production, not a moral blueprint, and that its basis is the materialist conception of history. It holds that capitalism's social production under private ownership produces crises and a proletariat, which takes political power, turns the means of production into public property and replaces market anarchy with a social plan, after which classes and eventually the state fade away.
scope: The doctrine Engels named "scientific socialism": the Marx-Engels theory of historical materialism and of socialism as the outcome of capitalist development, set against "utopian" socialism (Britannica, Encyclopedia.com, Merriam-Webster). It is represented by Engels's Socialism: Utopian and Scientific (1880), drawn from Anti-Dühring (1878), and the Communist Manifesto (1848). It excludes the Soviet official ideology that took the label later (Encyclopedia.com: its content varied with Soviet policy) and Leninist, Stalinist and Maoist doctrines. Marx and Engels are key figures of Marxism, so they are not listed here.

sources.title: Manifesto of the Communist Party, chapter 2: Proletarians and Communists
sources.author: Karl Marx and Friedrich Engels (1848)
sources.usedFor: Abolition of bourgeois property, wage labour, the ten measures, proletarian rule.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: The Manifesto calls for centralising credit in the hands of the State by a national bank with State capital and an exclusive monopoly, the opposite of free money.

abolish-income-tax.rationale: The Manifesto names the income tax itself as a tool, listing it among the measures the proletariat applies after taking power.

abolish-wage-labour.rationale: The Manifesto says there can no longer be any wage-labour when there is no longer any capital, and Engels says the proletarian revolution ends the wage-worker's condition.

alienated-labor.rationale: The Manifesto says that under capital living labour is merely a means to increase accumulated labour and the labourer lives merely to increase capital; Engels says the product becomes an instrument of the worker's subjugation.

all-land-state-owned.rationale: The Manifesto lists abolition of property in land with all rents applied to public purposes, and State-owned instruments of production, though it leaves small peasant property to be destroyed by industry rather than abolished.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Engels says capitalism's contradiction between socialised production and private appropriation ends in recurring crises and must come to an end, and Encyclopedia.com says the doctrine held that capitalism would inevitably be overthrown.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Engels says the bourgeoisie developed the productive forces with a rapidity unheard of before and that the possibility of a sufficient and free existence for all is now here for the first time.

central-planning.rationale: Engels says social anarchy of production gives place to a social regulation of production upon a definite plan, which makes a practically unlimited increase of production possible, and the Manifesto calls for a common plan under State-owned production.

character-from-environment.rationale: The Manifesto says man's consciousness changes with every change in the conditions of his material existence and social relations.

class-collaboration.rationale: The Manifesto's immediate aim is the overthrow of the bourgeois supremacy and conquest of political power by the proletariat out of an existing class struggle.

class-struggle-history.rationale: The Manifesto says the history of all past society has consisted in the development of class antagonisms, and Britannica describes class struggle as a driving force of history for scientific socialism.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: Engels says that in taking the means of production the proletariat abolishes all class distinction and class antagonisms, and the Manifesto expects classes to disappear once the ruling-class stage has run its course.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Engels calls the struggle for existence under capitalism a Darwinian struggle that socialised production ends, and the Manifesto makes class struggle, not struggle between peoples, the driver of history.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Engels calls the utopians' new social systems imposed by propaganda and model experiments foredoomed to remain utopian, and bases scientific socialism on class struggle and social ownership.

country-wealth-only-from-land.rationale: Engels says the wealth of modern society rests on the productive forces developed by industry under capitalism, not on land alone.

decent-living-guarantee.rationale: Engels says socialised production makes possible an existence fully sufficient materially for every member of society.

defeat-communism.rationale: The Manifesto states the Communist aim of overthrowing bourgeois supremacy and abolishing private property, so putting its defeat first is the opposite position.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: The Manifesto has the proletariat organised as the ruling class use despotic inroads on bourgeois property until class distinctions disappear, calling political power the organised power of one class for oppressing another.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Engels says production will be regulated upon a definite plan according to the needs of the community and of each individual, securing every member an existence fully sufficient materially.

flat-income-tax.rationale: The Manifesto lists a heavy progressive or graduated income tax, a rate that rises with income, not one flat rate for all.

gradual-change.rationale: The Manifesto calls the Communist revolution the most radical rupture with traditional property relations and has the proletariat sweep away the old conditions of production by force, though some measures proceed by degrees.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Engels says the capitalist has no social function beyond pocketing dividends, and the Manifesto says those who acquire anything do not work under bourgeois property.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Engels says capitalist industry developed the productive forces with unheard-of rapidity and created for the first time the possibility of an existence fully sufficient for all.

labour-priority-over-capital.rationale: The Manifesto says that in Communist society accumulated labour is only a means to widen and enrich the labourer's existence, the present dominating the past.

legal-duty-to-work.rationale: The Manifesto lists equal liability of all to work and the establishment of industrial armies among its measures.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Engels calls production for exchange anarchy that ends in periodic crises, and says socialised production replaces it with social regulation upon a definite plan.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Engels says the final causes of all social changes and political revolutions are to be sought in changes in the modes of production and exchange, not in men's brains.

means-match-ends.rationale: The Manifesto says the first measures can be effected only by despotic inroads on the rights of property, which lead on to a classless association, so the means differ from the end.

municipal-property.rationale: The Manifesto centralises all instruments of production in the hands of the State, and Engels has society as a whole take possession of the productive forces.

nation-first.rationale: The Manifesto says national antagonisms are vanishing, that united action of the leading civilised countries is a first condition of the proletariat's emancipation, and that ending exploitation of individuals ends hostility between nations.

night-watchman-state.rationale: The Manifesto has the State centralise credit, communications and transport and own and plan production.

no-central-bank.rationale: The Manifesto calls for a national bank with State capital and an exclusive monopoly over credit.

no-transition-to-communism.rationale: The Manifesto has the proletariat organised as the ruling class use despotic measures before class distinctions disappear, and Engels has a proletarian state that dies out only afterwards.

parliamentary-road-socialism.rationale: The Manifesto speaks of winning the battle of democracy as the first step, yet says the proletariat by means of a revolution sweeps away the old conditions of production by force.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: The Manifesto says Communists do not abolish personal appropriation of the products of labour for the maintenance of life, and only the social character of property changes when capital becomes common property.

political-violence-legitimate.rationale: The Manifesto says the proletariat, by means of a revolution, sweeps away by force the old conditions of production, and the dictionary definition says the goals are achieved usually by violent means.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Engels, quoting Marx, traces the accumulation of misery to the capitalist accumulation of capital and the industrial reserve army, not to population growth.

positive-liberty.rationale: Engels says socialised production makes possible an existence guaranteeing all the free development of their faculties, the ascent from the kingdom of necessity to the kingdom of freedom, and the Manifesto dismisses bourgeois freedom of buying and selling.

power-shapes-accepted-knowledge.rationale: The Manifesto says the ruling ideas of each age have ever been the ideas of its ruling class and that jurisprudence is the will of that class made into law.

production-for-use.rationale: Engels says social regulation of production will be according to the needs of the community and of each individual, replacing anarchic commodity production, and the Manifesto says accumulated labour becomes a means to enrich the labourer's existence.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Engels says the owners of the means of production appropriate a product that is exclusively the product of the labour of others, and the Manifesto says capital exploits wage-labour.

property-fundamental.rationale: The Manifesto says the theory of the Communists may be summed up in the single sentence 'Abolition of private property' and calls for despotic inroads on the rights of property.

public-ownership.rationale: Engels says the proletariat seizes political power and turns the socialised means of production into public property, and the Manifesto lists centralising all instruments of production in the hands of the State.

revolution-legitimate.rationale: The Manifesto has the proletariat make itself the ruling class by means of a revolution that sweeps away the old conditions of production by force, and Engels presents the proletarian revolution as the solution of capitalism's contradictions.

small-step-social-reform.rationale: The Manifesto has the proletariat make itself the ruling class by revolution and sweep away the old conditions of production by force, not work within established institutions.

social-market-economy.rationale: Engels says state ownership and capitalist relations do not solve capitalism's conflict, and that production of commodities is done away with when society takes the means of production.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: Engels says the proletariat seizes political power and turns the means of production into public property, and the Manifesto makes conquest of political power by the proletariat the immediate aim.

socialism-one-country.rationale: The Manifesto says united action of the leading civilised countries at least is one of the first conditions for the emancipation of the proletariat.

socialized-markets.rationale: Engels says that with society's seizure of the means of production, production of commodities is done away with, so a market of worker-owned businesses is not the aim.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Engels says the modern state, whatever its form, is essentially a capitalist machine, and the Manifesto says political power is merely the organised power of one class for oppressing another.

state-directs-investment.rationale: The Manifesto has the State centralise credit in a national bank and extend factories and instruments of production owned by the State in accordance with a common plan.

state-harmful.rationale: Engels says the state is not 'abolished' but dies out once classes are gone, and mocks the anarchists' demand to abolish it out of hand, while also expecting it to become unnecessary and wither away.

tax-inheritance.rationale: The Manifesto lists the abolition of all rights of inheritance among its measures, which goes beyond heavy taxation of large inheritances.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: The Manifesto lists a heavy progressive or graduated income tax among the measures generally applicable in the most advanced countries.

taxation-theft.rationale: The Manifesto lists a heavy progressive income tax among its own measures.

traditional-family.rationale: The Manifesto says the bourgeois family rests on capital and private gain and will vanish with capital, and it proposes replacing home education by social education.

vanguard-party.rationale: The Manifesto calls the Communists the most advanced and resolute section that pushes forward all others, yet says they form no separate party opposed to other working-class parties and set up no sectarian principles.

wages-fall-to-bare-minimum.rationale: The Manifesto says the average price of wage-labour is the minimum wage, and Engels says the reserve army regulates wages to the low level that suits capital.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: The Manifesto says the real aim is to do away with the status of women as mere instruments of production, and that abolishing the present system of production abolishes prostitution.

workers-nation.rationale: The Manifesto says the working men have no country and that Communists bring to the front the common interests of the entire proletariat independently of all nationality.

workers-own-party.rationale: The Manifesto speaks of the Communists as one among the working-class parties whose common aim is forming the proletariat into a class and winning political power.

notes: Adherents differ on how far Engels's 1895 emphasis on legal, electoral methods holds against his earlier view of revolution; answers on revolution follow the main line of both texts. The label was later claimed by Leninist and other regimes, which would answer party, army and state questions differently.
